purpose: Define a safe stale-artifact doctrine, audit known stale and transitional project artifacts, and stage retirement rules without deleting, purging, promoting, compiling, installing, or publishing anything.

doctrine.definition_of_stale: An artifact is stale when its operational claims, active references, branch/source coordinates, package identity, security boundary, runtime dependency, or promotion semantics are superseded by newer crowned or canonical doctrine. Age alone never makes an artifact stale.

artifact_classes.ACTIVE_CANONICAL: Current authority or required live reference. Never purge as stale.
artifact_classes.ACTIVE_CANONICAL_TRANSITIONAL: Current live reference that still contains a transitional dependency or superseded implementation detail. Migrate before retirement.
artifact_classes.ACTIVE_DRIFTED_GUIDANCE: Documentation or agent guidance that can actively steer work toward superseded architecture. Patch or clearly demote.
artifact_classes.ACTIVE_DRIFTED_EXECUTABLE: Script, workflow, test, guard, or runtime logic that enforces superseded architecture. Highest cleanup priority, but migrate before deletion.
artifact_classes.COMPATIBILITY_PINNED: Legacy implementation still referenced by canonical compatibility pointers. Preserve until replacement and green proof.
artifact_classes.HISTORICAL_EVIDENCE: Build receipts, hashes, signatures, past source-of-truth snapshots, device proof, or audit records. Preserve read-only.
artifact_classes.HISTORICAL_GUIDANCE: Old instructions useful only for archaeology. Move or label historical after references are removed.
artifact_classes.SOURCE_CANDIDATE: Current candidate not yet canonical. Do not call stale merely because it is unmerged.
artifact_classes.PROPOSED_MUTATION: Proposal awaiting human decision. Preserve until accepted, superseded, or explicitly abandoned.
artifact_classes.TEST_HARNESS_ONLY: Behavior or compatibility harness. Keep isolated from release source and runtime dependencies.
artifact_classes.QUARANTINE: Unknown provenance, conflicting payload, or unresolved licensing/security status. No execution or promotion.
artifact_classes.RETIREMENT_CANDIDATE: No longer referenced by active canonical code/doctrine, replacement is green, evidence retained, and cleanup gates are satisfied.
artifact_classes.DELETE_CANDIDATE: Retirement candidate with explicit Professor approval for deletion. This class may not be assigned automatically.

staleness_tests: Does the artifact contradict a newer crowned source-of-truth contract?
Does it point to a retired branch, package ID, donor, signer model, runtime dependency, or release path?
Can an agent, CI workflow, guard, script, or human following it still mutate the project incorrectly?
Is it still referenced by canonical code, manifests, workflows, tests, docs, or release gates?
Is it historical evidence or provenance that must remain available?
Has a replacement passed syntax/tests/CI and, when relevant, APK signing and physical-device gates?
Would removal break rollback, reproducibility, licensing attribution, or forensic auditability?
